Assess convergence of a runjags model

Source: R/JAGS-convergence.R
JAGS_check_convergence.Rd

Checks whether the supplied runjags-package model satisfied convergence criteria. Derived-draw views are refused with BayesTools_draws_view_inference_unavailable (also BayesTools_draws_view_unavailable); assess fit$original_fit.

JAGS_check_convergence(
  fit,
  prior_list = NULL,
  max_Rhat = 1.05,
  min_ESS = 500,
  max_error = 0.01,
  max_SD_error = 0.05,
  add_parameters = NULL,
  fail_fast = FALSE,
  check_indicators = FALSE,
  monitor = NULL,
  allow_not_assessable = FALSE
)

Arguments

fit

a 'BayesTools_fit' object created by JAGS_fit() with this version of BayesTools. Fits without its parameter map and fit contract (such as fits created by BayesTools 0.3.0) must be refitted: they stop with an error of class BayesTools_refit_required (see JAGS_validate_fit_contract()).

prior_list

optional named list of prior distributions (names correspond to the parameter names). When supplied, it must be the prior list stored with fit (attr(fit, "prior_list")); another list is an error. The classification of the fitted parameters always comes from the convergence roles of the fit's coordinates (see Details), not from this argument.

max_Rhat

maximum R-hat error for the autofit function. Defaults to 1.05. R-hat is the larger of the point estimate and the upper confidence limit of the potential scale reduction factor (coda::gelman.diag()), whereas the summary tables show the point estimate; the Rhat column of the diagnostics attribute holds the same value. With one chain, this criterion is skipped with a warning; the remaining enabled criteria are still assessed.

min_ESS

minimum effective sample size. Defaults to 500.

max_error

maximum MCMC error. Defaults to 0.01.

max_SD_error

maximum MCMC error as the proportion of standard deviation of the parameters. Defaults to 0.05.

add_parameters

vector of parameter names that are excluded from the default selection. Parameters named in monitor are checked even when they are listed here. Automatic fitting in JAGS_fit() and JAGS_extend() excludes nothing through this argument; it uses the default selection described in Details.

fail_fast

whether the function should stop after the first failed convergence check.

check_indicators

whether model indicator variables should be included in convergence checks. Binary indicators are checked as Bernoulli occupancies and categorical indicators are checked separately for every observed state. When monitor is supplied, eligible indicators are added to that selection. Defaults to FALSE.

monitor

optional character vector selecting parameters for convergence checks. A base name selects all of its indexed elements. A name that is not available stops with an error of class BayesTools_parameter_not_found. During automatic fitting, base names are checked against the monitored nodes before sampling, whereas an indexed request such as "mu[2]" is resolved against the fitted columns after the first run and fails then when the element does not exist. Requests are resolved against the monitored parameters that the summary tables show, including derived and auxiliary ones that the default selection leaves out. Private implementation nodes that the summary tables hide cannot be requested. NULL selects the default parameters; character() requests no parameters.

allow_not_assessable

whether requested sampled parameters with undefined diagnostics may be ignored. Defaults to FALSE. A sampled column that never changes when its chains are pooled, including a constant model indicator, is not evidence of convergence and remains not assessable, as does a diagnostic whose computation failed. A diagnostic computed on draws that vary is a value, not an undefined result, and is assessed even when it is infinite or zero: chains that are each constant but at different values give an R-hat of Inf and an ESS of 0, which fail max_Rhat and min_ESS whatever this argument is. Their MCMC error (the standard error SD / sqrt(ESS) of an ESS of 0) is Inf, so max_error and max_SD_error fail as well.

Value

JAGS_check_convergence returns a boolean indicating whether all requested, assessable parameters satisfy the enabled criteria. An explicitly empty monitor returns logical(0) rather than claiming convergence. When no parameters remain available (empty sample columns and no structural parameters) or the selection is empty, the function returns TRUE: there is nothing assessable, which is treated as vacuously satisfied. The diagnostics attribute contains one row per available parameter and classifies it as "assessable", "structural_constant", "not_assessable", "not_requested", or "not_checked" when fail_fast = TRUE stops before reaching that parameter. Its Rhat column is the larger of the point estimate and the upper confidence limit of the potential scale reduction factor (see max_Rhat). The errors attribute carries the failed checks: one message per failed criterion, with the most extreme value, as in BayesTools 0.3.0 (for example "R-hat 1.234 is larger than the set target (1.05)."), followed by the sentence "Failing parameters: 'mu', 'tau'." that names the failing parameters (the first five and the number of the others), and one message for every parameter whose enabled diagnostics are not assessable.

Details

JAGS_fit() assigns every fitted coordinate one convergence role, stored in the convergence_role column of parameter_coordinates() and derived from the declared model, never from the draws:

"sampled"

stochastic parameters, including the user's add_parameters that depend on a stochastic node; checked by default.

"indicator"

declared model indicators of mixture, spike-and-slab, and variance-allocation priors; checked with check_indicators = TRUE.

"structural"

declared constants: point priors, one-state indicators, reference and fixed publication-weight bins, a p-hacking kind shared by every mixture branch, the point total of an ordered prior and the coefficients it fixes, unit correlation diagonals and Cholesky constants, monitored fully observed data, and monitored deterministic nodes (<- or =) whose ancestors in the model syntax are all data or constants. They are reported as "structural_constant".

"derived"

deterministic functions of sampled nodes that BayesTools generates for formulas (such as random-effect correlation matrices, their Cholesky factors, and derived latent effects or SDs) and point priors whose location is an expression; checked only when named in monitor.

"auxiliary"

inclusion probabilities and the backend anchor of models without monitored parameters, checked only when named in monitor, and private implementation nodes that the summary tables hide (such as Dirichlet gamma draws), which are never checked.

Mirrored two-sided publication-weight bins are hidden in the same way. The default selection (monitor = NULL) consists of the sampled and structural parameters, and of the indicators when check_indicators is set. Automatic fitting in JAGS_fit() and JAGS_extend() uses the same selection.

See also

JAGS_fit() parameter_coordinates()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# simulate data
set.seed(1)
data <- list(
  x = rnorm(10),
  N = 10
)
data$x

# define priors
priors_list <- list(mu = prior("normal", list(0, 1)))

# define likelihood for the data
model_syntax <-
  "model{
    for(i in 1:N){
      x[i] ~ dnorm(mu, 1)
    }
  }"

# fit the models
fit <- JAGS_fit(model_syntax, data, priors_list)
JAGS_check_convergence(fit)
} # }
